comment: How `memphis_classify` turns the caller's `criteria` into the options a question is asked over. Both arms read THIS file: TypeScript (src/mcp/tools/classify.ts, `normalizeClassifyOptions`) and Rust (crates/memphis-operator/src/chat_basal.rs, `normalize_classify_criteria`). The runners are tests/unit/classify-criteria-contract.test.ts and crates/memphis-operator/tests/classify_criteria_contract.rs. WHY: the registry declares `criteria` as a UNION — an object of labels, or an array of 2-10 labels — and the native arm accepted only the object, so a model that had learned the array form on Telegram got a refusal in the cockpit. ONE normalisation, checked from both sides, is the fix; two copies of the rule are the bug. The object cases use keys that are ALREADY in sorted order: the gateway keeps an object's insertion order and a serde_json::Map is sorted, so an object whose keys are not sorted is the one case where the arms differ — and then only under `orders: 1`, the mode the BASAL service documents as order-sensitive. That difference is recorded in docs/adr/012-one-tool-contract-across-the-bridge.md, not hidden here.

cases.name: a score question over an array gets ordinal keys
a score question over an object keeps its keys
a non-string description is stringified, not dropped
an empty key is filtered out
an empty label in an array is filtered out
a single option carries no decision
cases.error: memphis_classify requires at least two criteria options

cases.name: eleven options are refused
cases.error: memphis_classify supports at most 10 options, got 11
